items.title: Euro FX futures drop to 1.1050 on policy divergence.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures declined 2% from Nov. 4 levels to 1.1050, reaching their lowest point since April 2025 amid sustained U.S. dollar strength. Market participants weighed diverging central bank rate expectations, with pricing reflecting additional Federal Reserve rate hikes into early 2027 alongside a more uncertain outlook for the European Central Bank beyond December. Meanwhile, the CME Group Euro CVOL index firmed toward month-to-date highs ahead of Friday's PPI release.

items.title: Nvidia CEO resigns as stocks pull back.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino breaks down Thursday's market action as U.S. stock futures move lower with Nasdaq-100 futures leading the declines following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. He examines potential ripple effects across data center financing, chip export restrictions and the broader indices, alongside higher 10-Year Treasury yields above 5%, a stronger dollar and pressure on metals and bitcoin. Bob also tracks crude oil's reversal lower after early gains tied to U.S.-Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz headlines, before previewing upcoming earnings, Federal Reserve speeches, eurozone GDP and U.S. PPI.

items.title: From GTA VI to Formula 1: why the future of investing could be entertainment
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Gaming, sports and live entertainment can turn loyal audiences into revenue streams that last for years. Unique franchises, global fan bases and experiences that are difficult to replicate can create lasting competitive advantages. Popularity alone is not an investment case. Profitability, growth expectations and the price investors pay still matter. The business of having fun On 19 November 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), one of the most anticipated video games in history, is scheduled to launch . Its publisher, Take-Two Interactive, reported exceptionally strong pre-orders this week and raised its annual revenue forecast. But for investors, the bigger story is not how many copies GTA VI sells next week. It is how much money the game could generate over the next decade.

items.title: Swiss Franc futures tumble to worst day since March.
items.excerpt: Swiss Franc futures declined sharply against the U.S. dollar, dropping 1.06% to an intraday low of 1.2040 to register their largest single-day percentage decline since March 2. Greenback strength expanded after core CPI increased 0.3% month over month, hitting the threshold Fed Governor Christopher Waller indicated would open discussion for a 50 bps move. The CME FedWatch Tool now fully prices a December policy increase, reflecting an 86.9% probability of a 25 bps hike and a 13.1% chance of a half-point adjustment. Meanwhile, the Swiss National Bank maintains its policy rate at zero with inflation remaining contained, setting up potential further policy divergence between the two central banks.

items.title: European defence stocks under fire: is the long-term investment case changing?
items.excerpt: Key takeaways US political uncertainty and Rheinmetall's weaker outlook have exposed growing doubts about defence companies' ambitious growth expectations. Europe's rearmament remains a structural priority , supported by rising military budgets and long-term security needs. Investors should focus on valuations, contract execution and cash generation rather than spending promises alone. After years of enthusiasm surrounding Europe's rearmament, the sector has come under renewed pressure. The Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections has raised questions about future American military spending, while Germany's Rheinmetall has disappointed investors with another reduction to its annual outlook.
